sentences.text: The victim female child was recovered from the vicinity of her house.
There is no evidence to show that extra-judicial confession was made by the applicant/appellant in a fit state of mind free from coercion.
It is further argued that medical evidence is not supporting the case of prosecution.
The learned APP oppose the application.
We have considered the submissions so advanced.
In fact, when the appeal was listed on earlier occasion, we made it clear that we are ready to hear the appeal finally.

Today also, we have shown our inclination for final hearing of the appeal, but the learned counsel for the appellant argued that he wants to work out the application for suspension of sentence and for releasing the applicant/appellant on bail rather than the final hearing of the appeal.
The victim of the crime in question is reportedly four years old female child.
Because of her tender age, she was not examined as a witness.
However, there are witnesses who had seen the victim female child sleeping in front of her house while Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1064 of 2017(16) dt.23-03-2023 the applicant/appellant sleeping near her.
P.W. 7 is father of the victim female child.
She was sleeping with P.W. 7 and applicant/appellant was sleeping just adjacent to them.
P.W. 1 is grandfather, P.W. 2 is grandmother, P.W. 3 is also a relative and P.W. 4 seems to be neighbour.
They all have deposed that applicant/appellant was sleeping in the vicinity of the victim female child.
Their evidence shows that in the morning hours, the victim female child was not found.
Similarly, the applicant/appellant was also not found present at the spot.
During search, the applicant/appellant was found hiding himself.
When prosecution witnesses apprehended him, he made an extra-judicial confession before them that he had committed rape on the victim female child.
Subsequently, the victim female child was also found.
She was subjected to medical examination.
P.W. 5 Dr. Sangita Verma, who had medically examined the victim female child found that there was lacerated wound at labia majora of the victim female child.
Her hymen was found torn.
It is not necessary that offence should be proved by direct evidence.
It can also be proved by circumstantial evidence.
In the case in hand the applicant/appellant was sleeping just beside the victim female child.

In the morning Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1064 of 2017(16)
dt.23-03-2023 hours, they both were not found.
Subsequently, the victim female child was found with her hymen torn and lacerated wound to her vagina.
Just coupled with extra-judicial confession was made use of by the learned Trial Court for convicting the applicant/appellant of the offences alleged against him.
It is urged before us that the applicant/appellant has undergone sentence of nine years and few months.
The appeal is ready for hearing and this Court was waiting for final hearing of the appeal.
However, learned counsel for the applicant/appellant had chosen to press his bail application.
The victim of the crime in question was four years old tiny-tot.
She was subjected to brutal rape.
Considering the nature of offence and the circumstances in which it was committed, no case for grant of bail is made out.
